text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- National statistics office INSEE's employment forecast for the first half of 1997 shows signs of slightly improving job creation rate. Unemployment rate is seen at 12.9 by the end of June.

-- Former European Commission president Jacques Delors in an interview calls for a reform of European institutions for clearer, faster and more democratic functioning. Worried by doubt over EMU, he adds it lacks a real economic policy program.
-- Banking sector unions call for a strike on April 4 against planned reform of a 1937 decree setting a strict framework for working hours and branch openings.
-- Renault to reshuffle distribution network, seeks to subsidise part of network on which it has direct control.
-- Total, Gaz de France and GEC Alsthom consider allying to build electricity plant in China.
-- Four bidders interested in buying Generale des Eaux health subsidiary Generale de Sante, estimated around seven billion francs.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Activity picks up slightly but unemployment remains high, INSEE report says.
-- Banque Vernes posts a 502-million-franc loss for 1996, after restructuring and heavy provision for real-estate related risks.
-- Thomson-CSF interested in Siemens Defense, according to Thomson company sources.
L'AGEFI
-- INSEE reports an improvement in the country's economic situation.
-- A merger between Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux would benefit both companies.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Foreign demand and a strong dollar partly account for economic pickup seen by INSEE experts, despite investment lag and continuing destocking.
-- Chrysler vice-president Robert Lutz says in an interview he does not rule out co-operation with other carmakers, notably on emerging markets.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Renault workers' conflict in a dead end at Vilvoorde Belgian plant which Renault plans to shut down.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Havas Advertising group seeks to strengthen U.S. business, to name an American chairman and CEO of Euro RSCG network, move headquarters to new-York.
